what: The schema form before and after it became Packed CBOR (draft-ietf-cbor-packed-19), on carsales of Cap'n Proto (the fields, types and value ranges of c++/src/benchmark/carsales.capnp, e866bdb), 20000 parking lots read in turn. Arm before: main 7a612a1, a map with keys in every struct. Arm after: the keys once in tag 113 as record function tags 114; every struct a record 128+i(9a nn nn nn nn [values]) with the fixed widths and offsets of before. encode: cbor::encode into a kept std::string; decode: cbor::decode<parking_lot>; read: cbor::view and at_path_compiled over every car, the sum of carValue of capnproto-carsales.c++. ns per car; bytes per car.
why: The owner asked for a benchmark of the schema form before and after it moved to Packed CBOR.
how: Google Benchmark, one binary per arm, each built twice (a, b), 3 rounds alternating, --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --benchmark_repetitions=3, random interleaving, GLIBC_TUNABLES trim_threshold, mmap_threshold and top_pad high.
finding: Medians before a / b and after a / b, ns per car: encode 57.8 / 59.2 and 48.9 / 49.6; decode 119.7 / 130.3 and 111.1 / 111.5; read 61.2 / 63.1 and 36.2 / 39.2. Bytes per car: before 471.8, after 174.4. A first run with a header whose record references had a wrong table index (the same length and work) gave encode 59.1 against 46.8, decode 121.6 against 104.3, read 60.5 against 34.3.

context.commit: mbedded-cbor main 7a612a1 (before) and the commit that holds this file (after)
